categories.main_business_segments: Micron operates through four primary business units: Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU), focused on hyperscale cloud customers and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for all data centers; Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU), serving mid-tier cloud, enterprise, and OEM data centers with memory and storage solutions; Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU), targeting mobile and client device markets; and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU), providing memory and storage for automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Micron's core technologies include DRAM (including DDR5, LPDDR, GDDR, and HBM), NAND (TLC, QLC, 3D NAND), and NOR flash memory. The company employs advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes such as EUV lithography, 3D stacking, and TSV for HBM, with production occurring on 300mm wafers in highly automated, cleanroom environments. Micron continuously invests in proprietary process and product technology to increase bit density, reduce per-bit costs, and improve performance, reliability, and power efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Micron's key customers are large hyperscale cloud providers, enterprise and OEM data centers, mobile device manufacturers, PC OEMs, automotive OEMs, and industrial/embedded device makers. Major end markets include data centers (cloud and enterprise), mobile devices (smartphones, tablets), client PCs, automotive (including ADAS and infotainment), industrial IoT, and consumer electronics.
categories.geographic_coverage: Micron operates globally with major manufacturing, R&D, and assembly/test facilities in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, the United States, Malaysia, China, and India. In 2025, approximately one-third of revenue came from customers headquartered outside the U.S., and about 80% of revenue was from products shipped to customer locations outside the U.S. Key sales regions include the U.S., Taiwan, China, other Asia Pacific countries, Japan, and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Micron is an integrated device manufacturer (IDM) operating primarily upstream and midstream in the semiconductor supply chain. It designs, manufactures, assembles, and tests memory and storage products, controlling much of its own wafer fabrication and packaging, while also utilizing subcontractors for certain processes and sourcing some components and materials from third parties.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Micron's strategic priorities center on technology leadership in memory and storage, with a strong focus on enabling AI and compute-intensive applications. R&D initiatives include advancing DRAM and NAND nodes (e.g., 1γ DRAM, G9 NAND), developing next-generation HBM (HBM3E, HBM4), new memory architectures, advanced packaging, and system-level solutions. The company is also investing in expanding U.S. manufacturing capacity (supported by CHIPS Act incentives) and modernizing global facilities to support future demand and innovation.
categories.revenue_model: Micron generates revenue primarily through the sale of memory and storage products (DRAM, NAND, NOR, SSDs, managed NAND, MCPs) to OEMs, hyperscale/cloud providers, and channel partners. Sales are made via direct sales, distributors, and online channels, with most contracts being short-term and pricing subject to market conditions. The company also earns revenue from licensing and, occasionally, technology/IP monetization.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Micron faces intense competition from global memory manufacturers such as Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Kioxia, Sandisk (Western Digital), ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), and Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC). While Micron is a technology leader in DRAM and NAND, it is smaller in scale than Samsung and SK hynix, and faces pricing and capacity competition, especially from Asian rivals. The company differentiates through advanced technology, U.S.-based manufacturing, and a diversified product portfolio.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In fiscal 2025, Micron reported $37.4 billion in revenue, up 49% from $25.1 billion in 2024, with net income of $8.5 billion and a gross margin of 40%. The company experienced strong growth driven by AI-related demand, particularly in DRAM and HBM, and improved profitability following a challenging 2023. Micron maintains significant capital investment, a robust cash position ($11.9 billion in cash and investments), and continues to expand manufacturing capacity globally.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Micron emphasizes technology leadership, high-performance and high-density memory solutions, and close customer collaboration to deliver differentiated products tailored for AI, data center, mobile, automotive, and embedded applications. Its value proposition includes advanced process nodes, power efficiency, reliability, and system-level integration (e.g., HBM, managed NAND, MCPs), as well as a commitment to U.S.-based manufacturing and supply chain resilience.
